2609.21149.title: Clinician-Grounded Quality Assurance for AI-Assisted Psychiatric Intake
2609.21149.paper_summary: Before patients can use AI-assisted psychiatric intake systems, health systems need practical ways to routinely evaluate these tools against their clinical standards for quality assurance. Because clinicians may use different intake styles, evaluation for this task must (1) support comparison across interviewing approaches, (2) minimize clinician burden, and (3) measure clinically relevant performance for health systems deploying these technologies. We present a clinician-grounded evaluation platform built around a memory-augmented patient simulator for open-ended AI interviewing, InterviewPlayground. We created interactive patients using InterviewPlayground with our expert-authored vignettes, constructed a simulated intake platform for the interviews, and designed evaluation modalities relevant to intake. In a pilot of 6 clinicians in a 25-minute assessment compared to a GPT-based LLM intake interviewer, the LLM recovered more of the clinically relevant items embedded in the patient vignettes (88.0% vs. 38.9%), but made more clinical inferences not based on the interview (56.8% vs. 27.8%), and characterized identified safety concerns less often (33.3% vs. 66.7%), setting the stage for deployed quality assurance for this task.
2609.21149.paper_summary_zh: 在患者能夠使用 AI 輔助的精神科接診系統之前，醫療系統需要實用的方法來定期評估這些工具是否符合其臨床標準以進行質量保證。因為臨床醫生可能使用不同的接診風格，因此這項任務的評估必須 (1) 支持不同訪談方法之間的比較，(2) 減少臨床醫生的負擔，並且 (3) 測量對於部署這些技術的醫療系統而言臨床相關的表現。我們提出了一個以臨床醫生為基礎的評估平台，圍繞著一個增強記憶的患者模擬器，用於開放式的 AI 訪談，名為 InterviewPlayground。我們使用 InterviewPlayground 創建了互動式患者，並利用我們專家的小品故事，構建了一個模擬接診平台以進行訪談，並設計了與接診相關的評估方式。在對 6 位臨床醫生進行的 25 分鐘評估的試點中，與基於 GPT 的 LLM 接診訪談者相比，LLM 從患者小品故事中恢復了更多臨床相關項目 (88.0% 對 38.9%)，但做出了更多不基於訪談的臨床推斷 (56.8% 對 27.8%)，並且識別安全問題的頻率較低 (33.3% 對 66.7%)，為這項任務的質量保證部署奠定了基礎。
